pointers.sentence: Text and bytes: `django/utils/encoding.py`

`django/utils/encoding.py` converts between text and bytes, with `force_str`, `smart_str`, `force_bytes` and `smart_bytes`, and between the forms a URL takes, with `iri_to_uri`, `uri_to_iri`, `escape_uri_path`, `filepath_to_uri` and `punycode`.
`force_str` makes its argument a `str` (`django/utils/encoding.py:force_str`).

With `strings_only=True` a value of a protected type is returned as it is too: `None`, an integer or a boolean, a float, a decimal, a date, a time or a datetime (`django/utils/encoding.py:is_protected_type`).
`smart_str` returns a `Promise` unchanged and passes anything else to `force_str` (`django/utils/encoding.py:smart_str`).
`force_bytes` makes its argument bytes, and takes bytes it is given to be UTF-8 (`django/utils/encoding.py:force_bytes`).
`smart_bytes` returns a `Promise` unchanged, as `smart_str` does: a lazy value whose result class is `str` comes back as itself, not bytes (`django/utils/encoding.py:smart_bytes`).

`django/utils/crypto.py` makes each salt, secret and value bytes with `force_bytes` before hashing ([Secret keys and `django.utils.crypto`](../security/keys.md)) (`django/utils/crypto.py:salted_hmac`).

`HttpResponseBase.make_bytes` does not use it for a response's body: its comment says `force_bytes` would re-encode bytes when the charset is not UTF-8 (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseBase.make_bytes`).

It leaves alone the reserved and unreserved characters of RFC 3986, which its comment lists, and `"%"`, which the end of RFC 3987's section 3.1 says must not be converted (`django/utils/encoding.py:iri_to_uri`).
So an escape passes through, and the function can be given a whole URL quoted in part, or its own result: Django's documentation calls it idempotent (`docs/ref/unicode.txt`).

With it Django escapes a redirect's target into the `"Location"` header in `HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__` ([The response object](../http/response.md#redirects)), the URL `HttpRequest.build_absolute_uri` returns ([Headers, host and scheme](../http/headers.md)), the prefixes of the static tags (`django/templatetags/static.py:PrefixNode.handle_simple`), a feed's links, and the `iriencode` filter's value ([The built-in filters](../templates/filters.md)).
`repercent_broken_unicode` then escapes again any byte that is not part of valid UTF-8, so the result always decodes (`django/utils/encoding.py:uri_to_iri`).

`repercent_broken_unicode` works in a loop, not by recursion, which its comment says is not to be used since the exception handling takes massive amounts of memory (CVE-2019-14235) (`django/utils/encoding.py:repercent_broken_unicode`).

The WSGI handler passes a request's path through it before decoding the path ([Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md)) (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:get_path_info`).

Its comment builds the safe characters from lists it calls RFC 3986's (whose reserved lack the `"#"`, `"["` and `"]"` of `iri_to_uri`'s), less `";"`, `"="` and `"?"`, after the RFC's section 3.3, keeping `"/"` because the whole path is escaped, not a segment (`django/utils/encoding.py:escape_uri_path`).

`HttpRequest._get_full_path`, behind `HttpRequest.get_full_path` and `HttpRequest.get_full_path_info`, escapes the request's path with it, and the query string with `iri_to_uri`, which leaves its escapes alone (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._get_full_path`).

The WSGI handler takes PATH_INFO to be unescaped already, as CGI defines it, and decodes only its UTF-8 (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:get_path_info`), and takes QUERY_STRING as it was sent, leaving its escapes to `QueryDict` (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.GET`):

`filepath_to_uri` makes a stored file's name the path of a URL (`django/utils/encoding.py:filepath_to_uri`).

`punycode` writes a domain in the ASCII form of internationalized domain names, with the standard library's `"idna"` codec: málaga.example becomes `"xn--mlaga-xqa.example"`, and an ASCII domain comes back unchanged (`django/utils/encoding.py:punycode`).

`get_system_encoding` returns the locale's encoding, from `locale.getlocale`, if Python has a codec for it, and `"ascii"` otherwise; its docstring cites tickets 10335 and 5846 (`django/utils/encoding.py:get_system_encoding`).

It runs once, at import, for `DEFAULT_LOCALE_ENCODING`, with which the management commands' `popen_wrapper` decodes an external program's error output (`django/core/management/utils.py:popen_wrapper`).
